sense: a maker’s name or mark on goods

terms.gloss: a brand, a make; a sort, a quality
evidence: Cic. Brut. 287: eae notae sunt optimae, those brands are the best (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The mark on a wine jar that told its vintage and quality, and so a brand of wine and any sort or quality of thing: secundae notae mel, second-grade honey (Col. 9.15.3; Lewis & Short). Its other senses are a mark or sign of any kind, a letter or shorthand sign, and the censor’s mark of disgrace.

evidence: Mart. 13.30.1: cāseus Etruscae signātus imāgine Lūnae
terms.comment: A mark or seal pressed into a thing; Martial’s cheese from Luna came signātus, stamped with the city’s moon, as Roman bricks, lamps and pots were stamped with the maker’s name.

phrases.latin: seu tē in remōtō grāmine per diēs fēstōs reclīnātum beāris interiōre notā Falernī
phrases.english: or whether, stretched out on the grass in some quiet spot on holidays, you treat yourself to a Falernian of an older brand

phrases.latin: cāseus Etruscae signātus imāgine Lūnae praestābit puerīs prandia mīlle tuīs
phrases.english: a cheese stamped with the moon of Etruscan Luna will give your boys a thousand lunches

sense.html: Lewis & Short: “a mark on a wine-cask, to denote the quality of the wine … hence, a sort, kind, quality”, and of notae in Cic. Brut. 287, “wines of those brands”. The use of a maker’s brand of anything else is ours.

sources: Lewis & Short: nota · Lewis & Short: signum
Quotation from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-martialis), checked against the editions named there. Horace checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (11 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
